name: Dr. Example referral
reach: a private link given to that sample provider's patients; it is not in the menus. On this example, the Site guide link at the bottom of any page opens a table that lists it
purpose: A private page for the patients of one referring provider: on this example a sample chiropractor, Dr. Example, who sends people with knee trouble. It greets the patient by the provider's name and says plainly what happens next, what it costs and who answers the phone, with no sales pitch and no promise.
owner_notes: One of four referral pages on this example, all built the same way: who sent you, three steps, three questions, the cost, who answers the phone, then three honest lines. Each named page has its own provider, its own body area and its own link to the matching Where it hurts page.

Dr. Erin Example, DC, of Example Family Chiropractic is a sample referrer, and the card is stamped Sample referrer. On a practice's own site a page like this carries a real provider who sends it patients.
It is written for someone who trusts the provider who sent them and knows little about the practice. It offers two ways forward: Book a video call, which opens the Booking page, and a call button.
The page says that, with the patient's permission, Dr. Example gets a note at each step. The website sends nothing to the provider; the practice keeps that promise itself.

Under Who answers the phone, beneath the hours, the page says: This website is not for emergencies. In an emergency, call 911. All four referral pages carry that line. It is part of the page itself, not a sample detail.
replace: The card at the top: the provider's name and letters, role, practice name, portrait and the note under What Dr. Example told us. All of it is a sample; a real provider's details go there.
The body area in the heading, your knee on this page, and the link Read about knee care first, which opens the Knees page. Both follow the patients that provider usually sends.
What it costs: your own from and to figures replace the sample range {{site.pricing.from}} to {{site.pricing.to}}.

Who answers the phone: your coordinator's first name replaces the sample {{site.coordinator.first}}, and your own number and hours replace the samples. The number shown, {{site.phone}}, is a sample and is also on the call button at the top.
keep: The answer to Is this approved, which starts with No: not FDA-approved to treat joints, and investigational for most uses.

The In one breath lines: not FDA-approved and investigational for most uses, results vary and none is promised, and if someone is not a candidate the practice says so and sends them back to their provider with notes.
The answer to What if I am not a candidate: the patient is told so on the call.
The small print at the bottom: statements not evaluated by the FDA, individual results vary, and the California notice unless your own lawyer confirms it does not apply.

top.say: The top of the page greets the patient by the name of the provider who sent them, Dr. Example on this example, a sample chiropractor, with a card about that provider and two buttons: Book a video call, and a call button.

what-happens-next.say: What happens next sets out three steps: a video call with a licensed clinician, an honest answer in writing, then treatment at home with follow-ups by the same team.

three-questions.say: Three questions gives short answers to what a referred patient asks first: is this approved, will it hurt and how long does it take, and what if I am not a candidate. A link there opens the Knees page.

cost.say: What it costs gives the range for one area, such as a knee or a shoulder, {{site.pricing.from}} to {{site.pricing.to}} on this example, which is a sample. It also names who answers the phone, and ends with a line that says the website is not for emergencies.

in-one-breath.say: In one breath repeats three honest lines, then offers Book a video call and a button to see the whole site.

questions.q: What is Dr. Example's page for?
alt: What does a patient sent by a chiropractor see?
What is a referral page for?
questions.say: It is a private page for patients a provider has sent to you. On this example the provider is Dr. Example, a sample chiropractor. The page tells that provider's patients what happens next, what it costs and who answers the phone, with no sales pitch.

questions.q: I'm a chiropractor. Is this what my patients would see?
alt: Is this the page a referred patient gets?
What would someone a chiropractor refers see?
questions.say: This is what a patient sees when a provider sends them to the practice the website belongs to. Here that provider is Dr. Example, a sample chiropractor. On your own site a page like this carries the real provider's name, portrait and note, next to your own price range.

questions.q: How does a patient get to Dr. Example's page? I can't see it in the menu.
alt: Why isn't Dr. Example's page in the menu?
Where is the chiropractor's referral page?
questions.say: It is left out of the menus on purpose. A patient opens it from a private link given to that provider's patients, and Dr. Example is a sample provider. On this example you can open it from the table of pages behind the Site guide link at the bottom of any page, or I can take you there.

questions.q: Where does the page show who sent the patient?
alt: Where is the provider's name and photo?
What is the card at the top of Dr. Example's page?
questions.say: At the very top. The heading names the provider, and a card there shows that provider's portrait, practice and a short note on the patients usually sent. On this example that is Dr. Example, a chiropractor, and the card is stamped Sample referrer.

questions.q: A chiropractor down the road wants to send me patients. How do I get that chiropractor a page?
alt: How do I get a referral page for a provider who refers to me?
Can my own referring chiropractor have a page like this?
questions.say: I don't have that. Your contact for the website can tell you how to ask for one. Each provider who sends you patients can have a private page like this sample one, and I can show you what goes on it.

questions.q: What do I change on Dr. Example's page?
alt: What do I replace on a referral page?
Is Dr. Example a real chiropractor?
questions.say: The provider. Dr. Example, the portrait and the note are samples, so a real provider who sends you patients takes that place. Further down, your own price range, the first name of whoever answers your phone and your number replace the samples.

questions.q: My chiropractor sent me here. What happens next?
alt: I was referred. What do I do now?
questions.say: The page gives three steps. First comes a video call of about thirty minutes with a licensed clinician, then an honest answer in writing: yes, no, or we need more information. If it is yes, a licensed nurse practitioner comes to your home for the treatment, and a physician oversees the plan.

questions.q: How much will it cost for my knee?
questions.say: The page says care is paid out of pocket, and a plan for one area runs from {{site.pricing.from}} to {{site.pricing.to}}. That range is a sample on this example site. Your exact quote is written down on the call, and a quote is never a commitment.
